subject: geom_vline draws line all the way to coordinate axis, whereas  geom_line won't do this

messages.author: 2a13147d4f12d038
messages.subject: geom_vline draws line all the way to coordinate axis, whereas  geom_line won't do this
parts:
geom_vline is very useful. However, I need to draw a line that does
not extend all the way across the entire graph but instead starts at
the bottom and extends up to a particular point.
I have used geom_line to do this
p<-p+ geom_line(data=threshLines, color='red')
which in the context of my program creates a graph like that shown at
the below URL:
http://www.psych.usyd.edu.au/staff/alexh/temp/geom_lineProblem.png

Unfortunately, geom_line does not truly extend all the way to the
actual axis line. Instead, it stops at the nominal axis limit (which
can be set by ylim()). Ggplot adds a little margin below the nominal
axis limit. Geom_vline is smart enough to draw the line all the way
into this margin. However it appears that geom_line cannot do so. If
there are data points below the axis limit, they get automatically
dropped I believe, along with triggering a message like "1: Removed 2
rows containing missing values (geom_path)."

How can I get geom_line to draw all the way to the very margin of the
graph, the way that geom_vline does?

Alex

messages.author: 2a13147d4f12d038
messages.subject: Re: geom_vline draws line all the way to coordinate axis, whereas  geom_line won't do this
parts:
I've discovered a work-around: use coord_cartesian to get rid of those
margins.

p=p+coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0.3,1))

So I should draw the lines up to the limits said by ylim() which
should be larger than I actually want. Then mask it down to what I
really want to show with coord_cartesian

--
